chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Do not speak when you stand for the Iqamah, for if you speak, you must repeat the Iqamah."

The Shaykh (Al-Shaykh Al-Tusi) said: And it is not disliked for a person to give the Adhan while sitting if he is weak in his body or if he is riding, and for similar reasons. And the Iqamah is not valid unless he is standing, facing the Qiblah, with choice.

key_terms.إِقَامَة: Iqamah (the second call to prayer, recited immediately before the prayer begins)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on speaking during the Iqamah and does it require repetition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that verbal speech during the Iqamah nullifies the call, necessitating its repetition, a ruling derived from the requirement of continuous, undisturbed recitation. Shaykh al-Tusi further distinguishes the physical conditions for the two calls, noting that while the Iqamah strictly requires the caller to be standing and facing the Qiblah, the Adhan permits sitting for the weak or those riding, reflecting the jurisprudential principle of ease (rukhas) in ritual obligations.
